lawyer:
B. K. Das, Advocate ----- in support of reference 
Md. A. Hannan, Advocate ----- in opposition of reference
parties:
Abdus Salam
Vs.
Musabbir Ali & Others
full_judgment:
A. S. Faizul Islam Chowdhury J:- This reference was made by Mr. S. H. Molla, Special Judge & Ex-Officio Additional Sessions Judge, Sylhet under which he recommended for setting aside the order dated 6.1.77 passed by Mr. Golam Mortuza, Magistrate, 1st Class and Resident Magistrate, Zakiganj in Misc. Case No. 22 of 1976. 

 2. The above mentioned Misc. Case No. 22 of 1976 arose out of an application under section 133 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 

 4. The learned Magistrate on receiving the application asked the opposite parties to remove the obstacles by 15-4-76 or to show cause. Subsequently the opposite parties showed cause and prayed for appointment of Jurors. The learned Magistrate himself appointed foreman of the Jury and he appointed four other members of Jury on nomination of the Jurors by either side. The Jury at first filed a petition before the learned Magistrate stating that they had compromised the dispute. But the first party Abdus Salam filed an application stating that second party was not carrying out the terms of compromise on which the learned Magistrate asked the Jury to go to the locality and to report if the parties carried out the terms of compromise, in default, action would be taken against the Jury for contempt of Court. Subsequently the learned Magistrate asked the Jury to show cause by the next date why proceeding for contempt would not be drawn up against them. Then the Jury submitted a report stating that the first party had no land and there was no reason to cause any damage to the first party on account of throwing of earth by the second party. On the basis of this report the learned Magistrate dropped the proceeding on 28-10-76. On 1-11-76 the first party filed an application stating it to be Naraji petition. In that petition the first party alleged that on the basis of a petition filed by the first party the Magistrate asked the members of the Jury to show cause, so the Jury became inimical towards the first party and submitted the second report against the first party. The learned Magistrate took up the case again and asked Sub-Adjutant of Ansar to inquire and report who filed report supporting the case of first Arty. But the earned Magistrate, relying on the second report of the Jury, passed order on 6-1-77 for filling the case. Hence the first party filed Criminal Motion No. 60 of 1977 in the Court of Sessions Judge, Sylhet which was heard by the Special Judge & Ex-officio Additional Sessions Judge who made the reference. 

 5. Mr. B. K. Das, the learned Advocate appearing to support the reference and Mr. Md. A. Hannan appearing to oppose the reference. Both of them agree that the Jury was illegally constituted. It was not constituted in accordance with the provision of Clause (a) of sub-section 1 of section 138 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. According to that provision the Magistrate himself was to appoint foreman and 2 members of the Jury on his own nomination and the other members of the Jury were to be appointed on the nomination of the second party. But the learned Magistrate appointed the foreman only on his own nomination and the other four members of the Jury were appointed on nomination by either side equally. So the Jury were not legally constituted and as such the award made by the Jury was not a legal and valid award. In the case of Muhadeo Lal and another v. Hossaint Pandy and others (1) the Jury was constituted in the manner just as in the present case. In that case it was observed, "Now quite clearly the nomination of a Jury is a nomination of the Court, which has to try the case and it would seem that irregularity with regard to that matter is an irregularity which goes to the root of the proceedings. Therefore, in my judgment it is doubtful whether in any event the provision of section 537, Criminal P.C., could cure the irregularity in this respect." In that judgment reference was made to the decision in the case of Upendra Nath Bhattacharjee v. Khitish Chandra Bhatrachlrjee. (2) In the latter mentioned case it was held that a Jury constituted in violation of the provisions of section 138 is not legally constituted, and is incapable of making a legally binding award. As the second party prayed for appointment of a Jury, the learned Magistrate was required to appoint a legally constituted Jury according to the provision of clause (a) subsection (1) of section 138 Cr. P.C. & then proceed with the case. Order of filing the case on the basis of the report of the illegally constituted jury cannot be sustained. 

 6. Hence, the impugned order dated 6.1.77 passed by the learned Magistrate is set aside and the learned Magistrate is directed to proceed with the case after appointing a jury as contemplated in clause (a) of sub-section 1 of section 138 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
